title: Stability of Matter in Lean: Lieb–Thirring, Ionization, the Thermodynamic Limit and Thomas–Fermi Theory
abstract: A Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of the stability of non-relativistic Coulomb matter in three dimensions. For normalized antisymmetric L2 electron states with q >= 1 spin states and static nuclei with charges between zero and Z, it proves a lower energy bound -C(q,Z)(N+M), uniformly in particle counts and nuclear positions. The main estimate is an additive inequality between nonnegative extended energies, valid even for infinite kinetic energy and nuclear collisions. A real quadratic-form theorem proves Coulomb finiteness and the lower bound for states with finite kinetic energy and distinct nuclear positions. The library also proves the kinetic Lieb-Thirring inequality with Rumin's explicit coefficient (9/35)(6 pi^2)^(2/3) q^(-2/3), Baxter's electrostatic inequality with its positive nearest-other-nucleus correction, and equality of the Fourier kinetic form with the classical Dirichlet integral on spin-valued Schwartz functions. The kinetic normalization is -Delta. The proof combines Pauli projections and Rumin's layer cake, a Voronoi boundary-measure proof of Baxter's inequality, nearest-nucleus screening, and Hardy's inequality. Three extensions prove the atomic bound N < 2Z+1 for weak ground states and strict binding, the unique continuous convex canonical zero-temperature energy density of neutral matter with finite-mass bosonic nuclei in Dirichlet balls, and the molecular Thomas-Fermi large-charge limit for arbitrary fixed spin and every fixed TF mass nu>0. Thomas-Fermi theory also has a unique relaxed minimizer, mass saturation at the total nuclear charge, and exact-mass attainment precisely up to neutrality.
